launches.body:
Hi there, I'm Connor from [Replicas](https://replicas.dev/) :)

Recently, you might have seen Stripe and Ramp release blogs outlining their in-house background coding agents. This showed us that background agents, with the proper tooling, can be relied on to ship critical production code.

Replicas is a background coding agent that can run your codebase locally.

We’re used by 20+ YC startups at all team sizes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99287&key=user_uploads/1688990/b35f4253-6fd0-478b-a04f-26f73a18b625)

**The Problem**

Background coding agents are a huge productivity boost for clearing tickets and shipping faster.

The existing solutions - CC/Codex on Cloud, Cursor Agents - lock you into one harness and give you **no control over the environment**.

This defeats the entire point of "background" agents. A powerful background agent should run everything locally, verify its work, and iterate until it's satisfied.

**How Replicas Works**

**Replicas** helps you delegate to as many background agents as you need:

\- Bring your own Claude/Codex credentials

\- Each agent gets a sandbox VM with your code cloned

\- The agent installs deps, spins up databases, runs services, and verifies its work locally

\- When it's done, it opens a PR for you to review

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99287&key=user_uploads/1688990/e20b6968-523d-4376-a05c-ba175cc61611)

Replicas can be triggered from Slack, Linear, GitHub (PR reviews, CI/CD failures), the Dashboard, or API.

The biggest difference is **Environments**. You can configure the following:

\- Files

\- Env vars

\- Start hooks

\- Warm hooks

\- Skills/MCPs

It's built so that its flexible to any kind of codebase, allowing Replicas to run everything locally just like a human engineer would.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99287&key=user_uploads/1688990/df185d7b-b90e-455f-9ff7-10dcefcfd8c7)

Replicas can also create **Previews**:

Meaning you can check out services (e.g web app on `3000`) running on the sandbox's VM from your computer with just a click :)

name: LightSprint
long_description:
Lightsprint is a collaborative software factory for product teams to plan visually, preview live and ship with an army of cloud agents. Your whole team, including non-engineers, can now ship end to end reliably.

The company is founded by Ben Ong, an AI investor who previously scaled AI products at SEA Group (NYSE: SE) and Temasek ($300B fund), Benedict Chan who was VP Engineering at Chainlink and CTO at BitGo (NYSE:BTGO), and Heng Hong Lee who built Facebook Messenger in 2013 and was Director of Engineering at Fazz (YC S17).
one_liner: Software factory for product teams

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Product changes (a copy tweak, a pricing page update, a new business logic update) often wait behind an engineering sprint. The PM files a ticket. Follows up in standup. Two weeks later, it ships.

Coding agents like Cursor and Claude Code made engineers 10x faster, but that speed never reached the rest of the product team. The PM still files a ticket and waits. The tools pitched at "non-technical builders" - Lovable, Replit - only spin up new prototypes from scratch. None of them touch the product you actually run.

Each of us hit this from a different side. Ben saw this bottleneck from the investor seat through his portfolio companies and during his time at SEA group as a PM. Heng Hong saw it from inside engineering: engineer time burned on changes anyone should be able to make. Benedict saw it from infrastructure: the plumbing to let non-engineers ship safely didn't exist yet.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Every person at a company will be able to ship product changes, not just engineers. The barrier between having an idea and shipping it disappears.   

PMs won't file tickets. Designers won't hand off mockups and wait. Founders won't choose between learning to code or hiring an engineer for a copy change. Engineering backlogs will shrink from bottleneck to review queue. Review comments get aggregated and fed back to the agent, which self-heals before an engineer steps in.

Engineers will focus on architecture, infrastructure, and the hard problems - while everyone else ships the changes they're closest to the customer to make. Software development becomes a team sport. We think this is as big a shift as when spreadsheets let non-finance people work with data, or when Canva let non-designers create graphics. Product agents will do the same for software.

launches.body:
**tldr:** We are building a collaborative platform for software teams to plan visually, preview live and ship with an army of cloud agents. Your whole team, including non-engineers, can now ship end to end reliably.

<https://youtu.be/P9e-5Mg72fc>

**The problem**\
Software is built by teams. But AI coding agents run alone on one developer’s IDE or terminal.\
The result: teammates are out of sync, planning stays buried in docs, and reviewers approve changes with little context. Execution has never been faster. But coordination has never been more painful. \
\
The SDLC was built around coding. Coding has changed, and the SDLC must be updated.\
\
**The solution**\
Lightsprint makes agentic software development collaborative. It completes the entire AI loop - not just code gen, but the full cycle from requirements to shipped code, with your whole team in the game.

1. **Visual Plan Mode**: Write a simple requirement. Lightsprint breaks it into a structured plan with tasks, dependencies, and visual options to choose from. Your whole team collaborates with the agent on the plan: see it, annotate it, and approve it. No more blind execution.
2. **Infinite Parallel Cloud Agents**: Hit execute and Lightsprint spins up multiple agents working your codebase simultaneously. One’s building the frontend component, another is building a dashboard, a third is writing tests. Anyone can steer the agent. What takes a team days gets compressed into hours.
3. **PR Preview Environments**: Every PR automatically gets a live preview URL. Not a diff. A running instance of the code. Your designer clicks through it and says “yes, ship it” or “change the layout” without reading a single line of code. Everyone on your team ships code now.

We’ve been using Lightsprint to build Lightsprint, and it has dramatically increased our engineering velocity. Lightsprint is also mobile-friendly so you can fire tasks from wherever you are. That has been a game-changer for us!

\
**About Us**\
The team is made of Ben Chan who was the previous CTO of Bitgo (NYSE: BTGO) and has led engineering teams of 300; Heng Hong, an engineering leader from Meta who built FB messenger; and Ben Ong, an ex VC who was part of the venture building arm at Temasek (300B AUM fund) and led products at SEA group (NYSE: SE). 

\
**Ask**\
If you're shipping with AI agents and want to improve coordination, accelerate feature development, or let non-technical teammates help build — we'd love to chat. Book a demo on <https://lightsprint.ai>

launches.body:
Hi, I’m Rob, the founder of Zenbu

## The problem

Coding agents are changing how software gets built, but they also create a new kind of complexity: running several agents in parallel, reviewing changes nobody wrote by hand, verifying their work, switching contexts, and keeping track of the codebase.

## The solution

Zenbu is an IDE for managing that complexity.

It’s built on top on Pi, the minimal, customizable coding agent. Around Pi, Zenbu adds an extensible IDE where everything is a plugin, including the tools for managing agents.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102484&key=user_uploads/3026245/3318eb29-4238-42d0-a338-9543b7e1fffd)

That matters because every developer and company works with agents differently. Instead of forcing one workflow, Zenbu lets the best solutions get built as plugins by developers and teams with their own needs. Over time, the best ways to work with agents become part of the shared foundation everyone can build on.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZUbY8zdv7Rc>

## About me

I build developer tools. I co-authored React Scan, an open source tool now at 22k GitHub stars and 800k weekly installs. I also worked at Vercel, where I joined the Next.js team and built an internal development environment.

Zenbu is the IDE I wanted for working with coding agents every day.

launches.body:
Hey YC! We're Nicolò and Arseniy, co-founders of Superlog ([superlog.sh](https://superlog.sh/)).

**TL;DR:** Superlog is the observability tool you're not supposed to open. A wizard scans your repo and instruments it with OpenTelemetry, and re-runs daily to keep your logs, alerts, and dashboards in sync with your code. When something breaks, an agent investigates with full context and posts one mergeable PR per incident into Slack.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AeX3pnHCMHg>

## **The Problem**

Arseniy spent years at Datadog, getting paged during the night to debug production incidents. In our first startups, we tried Sentry, Datadog, Grafana, Dash0, and nothing was good enough. 

* **Setup never ends.** Proper telemetry takes days of manual work and breaks the moment you ship new features. Half the dashboards end up empty or outdated.
* **Alert fatigue is constant.** Sentry floods Slack with duplicates and no context. The Saturday #ops ping is the worst feeling of the week.
* **The bill climbs.** Datadog invoices keep growing while engineers still spend hours configuring dashboards, chasing three AWS metrics that disagree, and copy-pasting stack traces into Claude at 11pm.

## **Our Solution**

**1. Telemetry that sets itself up.** Tell your agent:

```
Run npx skills add superloglabs/skills --all and use the skills to install Superlog in this project
```

This skill instruments your code with native OTel SDKs: proper semantic conventions, service and environment tagging. We cover all failure modes, endpoint performance, usage per tenant, and LLM/upstream cost (by callsite, tenant, and model). We run observability check-ins that keep adding logs, alerts, and dashboards as your code grows.

**2. An agent that investigates and ships PRs.** Errors get prioritised and grouped into incidents. The agent investigates with full context (logs, traces, metrics, recent deploys) and either produces a short tested PR, or posts its findings and pulls in the engineers who own the system (based on docs, prior investigations, Slack threads). One mergeable PR per incident in Slack. Merge it, ignore it, or open it as a Claude Code/Codex session and tweak.

**3. No alert fatigue.** Our custom eval setup makes sure incident summaries in your #ops channel are dense and correct, with severity and impact upfront. Every LLM-enhanced metric ships with a confidence score, so wrong guesses don't get boosted.

The telemetry you get is vendor-neutral: you keep all the OTel logs, metrics, and traces we install, even if you choose to switch providers.

## **Where We're Going**

Every engineering team in the world burns nights and weekends debugging production. We want to delete that loop. Observability should install itself, alert intelligently, and fix what it can.

## **About Us**

* **Nicolò (CEO)** — ex-BCG, math olympiad winner, scaled two startups to millions in ARR, with international enterprise contracts at Bluco (McDonald’s, Volkswagen, Dufry, etc).
* **Arseniy (CTO)** — coding since 12yo, won school olympiads, worked on high-performance data systems at Datadog and built engineering teams from scratch at Bluco.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101239&key=user_uploads/1660276/b630a0c3-d186-4f4c-95c0-6832f7893f47)

## **Our Ask**

We'd love intros to:

* Engineering leaders drowning in Sentry alerts or Datadog bills
* Startups that rolled their own observability and want to throw it away

**Try it:** [superlog.sh](https://superlog.sh/)\
**Email:** [nicolo@superlog.sh](mailto:nicolo@superlog.sh)

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Simi is the fastest, easiest, and most cost-effective way to create whiteboard explainer videos. You give it a prompt or a document. It writes the script, draws the illustrations, animates them, adds narration, and hands you a finished video in seconds. Anything from a one minute short to a full hour, in one shot, in 80+ languages. Built by Lamina Labs (YC P26). Use it through the app or the API for training, onboarding, product walkthroughs, sales, marketing, and education at <https://laminalabs.ai>.

Here is an explainer video about Lamina Labs: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RLuOCdamcHE>

## Why we built this

AI video right now is built to look like a movie, not to explain something.

But most of the video people actually need at work is the boring kind. A training module. An onboarding flow. A walkthrough of the feature you shipped last week. And making one of those is absurdly slow. You either pay an agency thousands of dollars and wait weeks, or you sit in a template editor dragging boxes around for an afternoon and it still looks like you dragged boxes around.

That is fine if you need one video. It falls apart the moment you need a hundred. A course. Every feature documented. Onboarding in every language your customers speak. Anyone who has priced that out knows the math does not work.

## How it works

You type what you want. Simi writes the script, draws and animates it, and gives you a properly narrated video in seconds.

That is the whole thing. No storyboard, no timeline, no boxes to drag. Type "explain how photosynthesis works," or hand it a long compliance doc, and you get a finished video, not a draft. And it does not choke on length. One minute to a full hour, generated in a single shot.

If your team makes videos, you should be using this.

## What people make with it

Training and onboarding videos from the docs you already have. Product walkthroughs, one per feature, updated as fast as the product changes. Sales and marketing explainers, in every market you sell into. Course and lecture videos in the Khan Academy style. Faceless YouTube channels and localized social video at volume. Agencies run it through the API to produce explainer videos for their clients.

## What makes it different

An agency gives you a video in weeks for thousands of dollars. Simi gives you the same video in seconds for a fraction of that. That is the whole pitch, and it is enough.

A few things worth knowing beyond speed. It generates anything from a minute to an hour in one shot. It speaks 80+ languages, so you write once and localize everywhere. And it is built to plug in. Use the app, call the API from your own product, or run it inside agent frameworks like OpenClaw and Nous Research's Hermes.

## Who we are

We are Sudip and Kartikesh, the founders of Lamina Labs, and Simi is the first thing we have built. We are both from Nepal. We met at MIT and started building together there. We are the first Nepalese founding team to go through YC.

Simi is named after Simikot, the Himalayan village where Sudip grew up. We started with education because that is where this problem hurt us personally. But it is everywhere. Any time someone needs to turn an idea into a clear picture, that is us.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104668&key=user_uploads/2592448/ddd4246e-1dae-4302-8e33-7c51d0264d6b)

## Our asks

If your team spends real money or real time making explainer, training, or onboarding videos, talk to us: [founder@laminalabs.ai](mailto:founder@laminalabs.ai)

We would love intros to L&D leaders, to agencies making video at volume, and to founders who want video generation inside their own product through the API.

And if you just want a video explaining your own startup, **try it:** <https://app.laminalabs.ai> \
**Learn more:** <https://laminalabs.ai>

Data is the lifeblood of modern finance. Every desk, every strategy, every edge starts with it.

Yet prediction markets, one of the fastest-growing asset classes in the world, still lack the tooling that makes every other asset class easy for desks to adopt, leaving anyone trying to use this data stuck with three major pains:

1. Fragmentation across venues with no shared symbology
2. No tick-level history to backtest against
3. Weeks spent normalizing data instead of generating signals

These compound the moment real money tries to enter, leaving a glaring problem to be solved.

launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re [Theodore](https://www.linkedin.com/in/theodore-otzenberger-895345131/) and [Louis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/louis-scremin/) - Co-Founders of [Armature](https://armature.tech/) 👋

### TL;DR

**Armature helps companies monitor, analyze, and optimize how AI agents experience their products.**

* We discover your product through MCP and CLI, **run the real workflows your customers’ AI agents do** and let you finally see your customers’ agents thinking **traces**.
* We provide analytics, run **benchmarks**, and turn this into **concrete actions** to improve your MCP and CLI.
* This is only the beginning: we are reinventing the building blocks of the ~~User~~ **Agent Experience**.

**_The Ask:_** _If you are building a product that is increasingly used by AI agents or if you want to ensure agents can use your product but don’t know where to start, we’d love to hear about your challenges! You can also try our product self-serve **for free** directly at [armature.tech](http://armature.tech)._

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Gtc5RzGxJ0>

### ❌ The Problem: The Missing Agent Experience (AX)

We have 30 years of tooling to optimize User Experience (UX), from session replays and funnel analytics to live support chat. But as products are increasingly operated by **AI agents** rather than humans, we lack the equivalent tooling for **Agent Experience (AX)**.

Right now, companies have **zero visibility** into how each agent (Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, OpenClaw, etc.) interacts with their products. And when a bad AX causes an agent to fail silently, the end-user simply churns.

But it goes deeper. As agents become the primary users, the fundamental mechanics of software products simply stop working. Because if a human isn’t looking at the screen:

* _How do you upsell a premium feature to an AI?_
* _How do you build brand loyalty with a user that doesn’t feel emotions?_
* _How do you offer customer support when an agent fails?_

We are building Armature to solve these exact problems and so many more questions related to this shift!

### 💡 Our Solution: Armature

Armature helps companies monitor, analyze, and optimize how AI agents experience their products.

**What we do today:**

* **Automated testing:** We run complex sessions against your MCPs/CLIs across all major harnesses and models to catch broken workflows before your users do.
* **AX analytics & benchmarking:** No more black boxes. We trace agent sessions to show you exactly what the model "thought", what context it missed, and why it failed. We measure your AX against competitors to ensure you remain the preferred platform for agents to use.
* **Auto-remediation:** Our MCP lets your internal coding agents plug into Armature to autonomously fix your product's AX based on our run data.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101594&key=user_uploads/3408440/5642c5dd-a3b1-46e1-865d-a0425ceba1d5)

**Our vision for tomorrow:**

Reaching full understanding of how agents use your product and how you can improve it is only step one. 

The next step is to provide the **foundational infrastructure for the Agent Experience**, powering agent-native revenue, lifecycle marketing, and customer support for the next generation of software.

### 🙏 Our Ask: If you’re building apps for agents, let’s talk!

1. **Audit your MCP or CLI:** If you are building for agents, you can start by running your first audit & benchmark on [**armature.tech**](http://armature.tech) **for free** to see how they actually experience your app.
2. **Let’s chat:** If you are facing challenges to make your app usable by agents or optimize the agent experience, please reach out to [**founders@armature.tech**](mailto:founders@armature.tech). We’d love to discuss and help you with this!

### 👬 The Team: why we are working on this

**The problem**

After my last company was acquired, I led our coding agents rollout and personally shipped 4+ full-stack products in the first 3 months. I then started enabling the rest of the team to do the same. But we hit a lot of friction fast: we needed to create working environments, we didn’t have any control or context to ensure agents contributed correctly, and nobody had visibility of what was being shipped. And because we'd gone deep on one provider's tooling, when their reliability dipped, the whole team slowed down.

Everyone rolling out coding agents across their team hits the same walls:

* **No environment setup:** No easy way to give engineering and product teams production-like environments where agents can safely run.
* **No guardrails:** No access controls, system instructions, or secrets management for agents.
* **No visibility:** No way to see what agents are doing, what they're changing, or where things break.
* **Vendor lock-in:** Go all-in on one model provider's agent infra and your whole team is exposed when reliability, pricing, or model quality shifts.

Without these, you end up either moving slower than your competition or causing major downtimes on your product.

**What we built**

Runtime sits between your team and the coding agents they use. It works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Copilot, and others, and can be called programmatically or used through Slack, Linear, Jira, Asana, Teams, CLI, and more.

\
Here's what that looks like in practice:

* **Environment templates:** Import any repo and set up a replica of your environments once. Our agents handle the setup for you, even for monorepos and microservices.
* **Sandboxed environments:** Anyone on the team can spin up a sandbox in milliseconds with a live preview of your product, make changes with their preferred coding agent, and open a PR.
* **Configurable guardrails:** System instructions, skills, allowlists, encrypted secrets, and role-based access control for both humans and agents.
* **Observability:** See exactly what every human and agent is doing across every interaction, down to the tool call and chain of thought.
* **One-click deploys / PRs:** Anyone can deploy from their sandbox. Coding agents auto-fix build errors and verify the deployment is healthy before it goes live. You control what gets deployed and can roll back or destroy deployments at any time.

Hey YC! We’re [Hang Huang](https://linkedin.com/in/hang-huang-oliver) and [Tony Chang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tony-chang-0430/) from [InsForge](https://insforge.dev/).

**TL;DR:** InsForge lets your AI coding agent deploy and operate the full backend (servers, database, auth, storage, and more) from one consistent CLI. Instead of stitching together separate tools and dashboards, your agent manage entire backend infrastructure end-to-end.

<https://youtu.be/7Bax5qz0IfM>

**The Problem**

The way software gets built is changing fast. Coding agents are now the primary builders, but every backend platform today was designed for human developers, with dashboards, manual configs, and workflows that require a person at every step.

We tried MCP servers like Supabase, Vercel, GitHub, and Context7, but kept running into the same problems: tools bloated the context window, payloads came back at 10K+ tokens, and core backend state like telemetry, configs, logs, and runtime behavior still wasn’t accessible in a way agents could reliably use.

**Our Solution**

So we built InsForge as one backend platform your coding agent can actually operate. Install our CLI and Skills with one command, and your coding agent can build, run, debug, and scale full-stack apps end to end on InsForge.

Every primitive returns structured outputs and readable errors the agent can act on. And because agents make mistakes, branching, scoped permissions, and reversible writes let you review or discard changes safely.

**Where We're Going**

We believe that coding agents won’t stop at writing code. They’ll run your entire application and infrastructure autonomously as well. For that to work, backend infrastructure needs to become agent-native: CLI-first, observable, permissioned, reversible, and designed around agents as operators.

**tl;dr: OpenRouter became the router for model spend; we're building that layer for agent capabilities, starting with paid tools: web search, scraping, extraction, enrichment, and more from top providers in each category. No provider accounts or API keys, one balance, pay per use. We benchmark every provider on real tasks and route each request to the one that performs best, with fallbacks when a provider fails. We're looking for early users to try it out with free credits, email us at [founders@amorphiclabs.com](mailto:founders@amorphiclabs.com) if you want to check it out!**

**Launch Video:**

<https://youtu.be/-dxc8ZAUfFc>

**The problem:**

Agents can only use the tools a human wired up in advance, and they won't tell you what they're missing: they quietly make do, failing at anything they weren't hand-equipped for. Even when you do the wiring, you're picking blind: nobody actually knows which search API is better for this query, or which scraper will survive this site. The "best setup" frontier moves daily, so keeping up means hours of trawling MCP directories, X threads, and blog posts. Agents stay only as capable as their setup, and the more autonomous they get, the more that ceiling costs.

**What we do:**

Your agent asks for what it needs ("structured data from this page", "research this with citations"). We route the request to the best provider for that specific task, based on benchmarks on real tasks and outcome feedback from the agents using them: success rates, result quality, latency, and cost. If a provider fails, we cascade to the next, so your agent gets a result instead of an error. Every request makes the routing smarter. One balance pays for all of it, and it's the same MCP whether it's your own coding agent or agents you're shipping in a product.

APIs are just the start. The same marketplace will let agents acquire skills, hire other agents for specialized tasks, and sign up for software directly through MCPs, all from one balance.

launches.title: Rindler - Turn Any Website Into An API For AI Agents
launches.tagline: Reliable web actions for AI agents, without integrations or scripts
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Rindler turns websites into deterministic APIs for AI agents. We map a site once into screens, actions, and structured outputs, so agents can read data and take actions quickly and reliably.

**Ask:** If you’re building an agent that needs to browse the web, compare products, fill forms, search listings, use authenticated portals, or act on third-party websites without an API, we’d love to help.

<https://youtu.be/V_nCIxYD-so>

## Problem

More products are starting to depend on AI agents that can do real work on the web: shop across retailers, pull housing listings, use job boards, submit forms, monitor prices, update back-office systems, and operate inside customer portals.

But most browser agents still treat every website visit like a new puzzle. On every run, they need to decipher the page, infer what matters, decide what to click, and recover when the page behaves differently.

That works for demos, but it breaks down in production. Real websites have pop-ups, login gates, cookie banners, bot defenses, slow-loading forms, dynamic filters, fragile dropdowns, layout changes, and pages that look similar but behave differently.

The result is slow execution, high token cost, and workflows that are hard to trust.

## Solution

Rindler maps websites into deterministic APIs for agents.

Instead of forcing an agent to re-explore a site every time, Rindler captures the site as structured screens, available actions, and typed outputs. Agents can then call actions like **search,** **add_to_cart**, or **download_records,** depending on the mapped site.

At runtime, Rindler handles the browser work through a remote MCP endpoint:

* Returning structured data
* Applying dynamic filters
* Managing popups, bot defenses, and layout changes
* Supporting authenticated flows

## Background

We started Rindler because “AI agent uses a browser” is compelling, but the current browser-agent loop is too brittle for teams building real products.

If an agent needs to use the same third-party site hundreds or thousands of times, it should not have to rediscover that site from scratch on every run.

Rindler is still a work in progress. Some sites map cleanly, others require more in-depth mappings, and bot-defended or logged-in sites may need a one-time credential or cookie capture.

We’re looking for feedback from founders building products where reliable web actions are part of the core workflow.

If there’s a website you wish your agent could use reliably, send it to us!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108274&key=user_uploads/2563241/28db62de-d65b-4498-84ac-12e2683c65f2)

**The Problem** 

In the next 10 years the best software startups will be those who can effectively deploy tokens. 

Right now that's significantly harder than it needs to be. If you’ve ever ran multiple agents locally you immediately know this pain.

Laptop crashes, wrangling gitwork trees, juggling ports, and more headaches.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108274&key=user_uploads/2563241/6f320e85-ccbb-4fb4-a5e9-6ec3cb0206c7)

So cloud is the obvious answer right? 

But setting up with these existing providers is quite a hassle, and oftentimes they miss some key feature that your local config has.

**What we do**

We deploy software factories into businesses that want to **tokenmaxx** but don't have the time or the resources to set up the infrastructure.

During onboarding, we transfer all of your local sessions and MCP servers to Hoplite, meaning you can pick up right from where you left off. We also configure all the required dependencies and CLIs that your projects require, letting you see instant previews of what your agent is doing.

Our bet is that as models improve, we’re going to start caring less about the code that they output (we’ll implicitly trust it), and shift our focus towards the product itself. Hence, a platform that prioritizes iteration on product rather than code will ultimately win. 

We also have an iMessage integration so you can prompt on the go.

We installed in our first business last week and we saw an immediate result, from sentry logs going from largely ignored to fully proactive PRs when something breaks. 

They have significantly faster iteration cycles and lower priority tickets have been continuously getting merged. 

They wanted faster iterations but didn't have the infrastructure to support a software factory, so we went in and built it.

If this sounds like you reach out! 

P.S. – If you love Vim, this is for you. It was built with keyboard navigation in mind 🙂

demo vid: <https://x.com/ryan_morr/status/2078240892738224292?s=20>

sign up: <https://hoplite.sh>

**How we got here**

Previously, we were building an agentic harness for financial markets; letting retail investors trade with AI. The product worked well, but we never truly had founder market fit. 

We found that our true passion was in talking to founders and developers – and oftentimes when pitching our old product, I’d spend 5x longer explaining our potential pivot 😅

And so we set out to commercialize a product that we’d built internally, one that’d let us deploy the $1.5 million in OpenAI credits effectively.

**Our Ask:** Let us Collison install! Bence and I will come to your apartment and set up everything for you (and bring some matcha & assorted sweet treats). We want to build the best possible product for developers to move faster and care deeply about peoples setups. Partially because we have very strong opinions of our own… 

**The Team** 

Bence & I are both from Ireland 🇮🇪. We met in college in a course called Immersive Software Engineering. 

We have been building projects & doing freelance work tg for the past 2 years, but got sick of building other people's visions. 

We previously interned at AWS (Bence) & [@Stripe](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/240) (Ryan). After that experience, we were fed up and decided to drop out to build. 

We are best friends & just want to build a product that people truly love.

launches.body:
**Palisade builds agents to run your online marketplace. Our agents have driven over $2.7M in GMV since the start of the batch.**

<https://youtu.be/cuVQHgQ9yHg>

**The problem:** The best marketplaces in the real world run on salespeople. The real estate agent who takes you house to house and texts you the moment the right listing is about to hit the market. The Sephora beauty advisor who finds your exact shade. The jeweler who walks you through diamond cuts for an engagement ring. **Online marketplaces skipped that person entirely** and left the selling to search bars and filters.

**What we do:** Palisade builds the missing **sales agent**. Every single visitor to your marketplace gets their own dedicated agent, and conversion goes up massively.

**How it works:** Agents can take any action possible on your platform. They know every listing, every UI component, and every flow. They navigate for users with their own cursor, help them discover, add to cart, and complete the purchase or booking. They build custom pages and reshape the UI around how each person actually uses the platform, remembering each user and tailoring the experience to their behavior and preferences. Each dedicated agent can naturally text and email with their customer as well.

**Is this another chatbot?** Each agent is proactive with much richer, customized components than an idle chatbot. It’s like giving every customer an omnipotent Claude embedded into the platform. Palisade agents get to know each customer personally and build relationships over time. They keep working after customers leave, remember them when they return, and reach out proactively over email and text with personal messages. And everything they learn flows back: agents aggregate their conversations into reports, insights, and recommendations for sellers, and offer to make concrete optimizations themselves, to the listings and even to the marketplace platform itself.

**Integration**: Start by adding just one line of code to your existing platform, whether your marketplace sells yachts, vacation rentals, rare collectibles, or anything else.

**Backstory:** After studying CS at Princeton, I spent years at Amazon building software for influencers to sell more products. I then became a founding engineer at Sage AI Labs, where I worked on some of the very first iMessage agents for consumer shopping. That work left me with a deep understanding of consumer habits and marketplace dynamics.

**If you’re looking to transform your marketplace:** Reach out at [jonathan@runpalisade.com](mailto:jonathan@runpalisade.com)

launches.title: Prized: A cloud devbox that feels local
launches.tagline: The fastest way to run coding agents in the cloud without giving up your local workflow.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Marinos and Hudson, co-founders of Prized.

**TL;DR:** Prized gives developers a dedicated devbox in the cloud that still feels local. Your files stay synced to a real folder, ports show up on [localhost](http://localhost), and coding agents keep running when you close your laptop.

Launch video: <https://youtu.be/JmaxNhEdLdc>

**The problem**

Coding agents can work for hours now. But only if you keep your laptop open.

You start a refactor, a migration, or a big build. Then you need to leave. Close the lid and the agent dies with it.

You can move everything to a VM, but now you're doing remote dev. Your files live somewhere else. Your ports need forwarding. Your terminal disappears when the connection drops.

Remote development still feels remote.

it shouldn't…

**The solution**

With Prized, one command puts your project on a dedicated devbox without giving up local development:

* **Real files on your Mac.** Prized syncs both ways into a normal folder, so everything keeps working the way it already does.


* [**Localhost**](http://Localhost)** stays [localhost](http://localhost)**. Servers running on the box appear on your Mac automatically, including loopback-only services and hot reload.


* **Sessions stay alive.** SSH lands in a persistent terminal session on the box, so disconnecting or closing your laptop doesn't stop the work.


* **Compute grows with the task.** Resize the box without rebuilding your environment or moving your project again.


* **Secrets stay out of the agent's hands.** For brokered secrets, the agent only sees a placeholder.

**The team**

We worked together at Gander (F24) building fleet management software for private jets. After the company's acquisition by Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR), Marinos continued school at Stanford, and Hudson went on to be an engineer at Suno.

We built Prized for ourselves after getting tired of having to keep our laptops cracked open all the time. A raw VM kept the process alive but gave up the local workflow we actually wanted.

Check Prized out at [https://prized.dev](https://prized.dev/), or reach out at [founders@prized.dev](mailto:founders@prized.dev).

launches.title: Prized: Lovable for internal tools
launches.tagline: The fastest way for non-engineers to ship secure internal tools.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Marinos and Hudson, co-founders of Prized.

**TL;DR:** Prized lets anyone at your company build and ship secure internal tools with AI. Company data comes pre-connected and scoped to what each person should see, every access is audited, and finished tools deploy behind your company's sign-in.

**Launch video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WILimoqemD4>

**The problem**

Building software has never been easier. And the people who need internal tools most, in ops, support, and finance, are done waiting on engineering.

So they build it themselves. They rip Claude Code or Cursor, pull straight from company data, and ship a working tool in an afternoon. No permissions. No audit trail. No one watching where the data goes.

Security is assumed to be fine because the tool is "just internal."

it's not…

**The solution**

People aren't going to stop building with AI. So we built them a place where it's safe.

With Prized, anyone can spin up a sandbox that comes with company data already attached, scoped to what they should see, with an audit trail on every access. 

From there it's whatever building style they like: describe the tool in our app builder and watch it take shape, or bring a coding agent like Claude Code and build it themselves. Shipping is one click, and the finished tool sits behind your company's sign-in.

The person who runs the workflow finally gets to build the tool for it. Safely, this time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105647&key=user_uploads/2485896/e426b427-8a79-4ca5-b462-b26b98db43e0)

**Secure by default**

Security is enforced in the infrastructure, not left to the person building the tool:

* **Least privilege per tool.** Every tool gets its own database role and integration scopes; it can read and write only what it was granted.
* **Credentials stay out of reach.** Secrets live in a broker and never touch the tool's code or the agent's context, so they can't leak or cross workspace boundaries.
* **Outbound traffic proxy.** External calls only go to explicitly allowed hosts, and integrations are read-only until someone turns writes on.
* **Admin visibility.** IT sees every tool in the org: who built it, what data it reads or writes, who can use it, and risky changes (like a destructive migration) need explicit approval before they ship.

**Your agent, our sandbox**

Already have a favorite coding agent? Bring it. It plugs into the same governed sandbox and ships the same way.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105647&key=user_uploads/2485896/fcfa68c5-8c9f-4d13-b37c-d526e733539a)

**The team**

We worked together at Gander (F24) building fleet management software for private jets. After the company's acquisition by Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR), Marinos continued school at Stanford, and Hudson went on to be an engineer at Suno.

**Our ask**

If any of these describe you, we'd love to talk:

* You work in ops, support, finance, or RevOps and keep waiting on engineering for small tools.
* You lead engineering and one-off tool requests keep eating your roadmap.
* You're in security or IT, wondering where AI-built tools are showing up at your company.

Check us out at[ https://prized.dev/](https://prized.dev/), or reach out at [founders@prized.dev](mailto:founders@prized.dev).

launches.title: Alkera - The data agent that you can trust
launches.tagline: Alkera is an agent that replaces your coding agent to reliably and safely perform real data engineering/analysis/science work.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Data teams adopting AI agents want speed, but one wrong step can quietly ripple through your dbt models, dashboards, and business decisions before anyone notices. [Alkera](https://alkera.ai) **is an AI data agent for data engineers/analysts/scientists or anyone who wants to gather data insights that actually understands your data stack** (column-level lineage, graph-based planning, and a living knowledge base), so it ships data work you can trust. It's **#1 on UC Berkeley's [DataAgentBench](https://ucbepic.github.io/DataAgentBench/),** which tests complex, data-oriented tasks.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fQEVpQPYNxg>

Coding agents can write data code that runs. **For data engineering, knowing it's correct is the hard part.** This is knowing that a transformation didn't quietly redefine a column three models downstream and corrupt the revenue dashboard that the exec team checks every Monday. **For data analysis and data science, beyond data access and lineage problems, coding agents struggle with highly parallel work spread across multiple machines.** When interacting with remote computing nodes, they do so only via fragile chains of SSH commands. Long processing and training runs have you more as a babysitter than a scientist.

**Alkera is a data agent that works natively across your entire data stack, with the context and guardrails coding agents lack.** Every change it makes to a query, transformation, model, or notebook is backed by a real understanding of your pipeline.

It's **#1 on UC Berkeley's DataAgentBench,** which tests complex, data-oriented tasks. You reach it through an IDE extension (VSCode, Cursor), a CLI, or the browser — wherever you already work.

What makes it different:

* **Column-level lineage across your data stack.** Trace a single row from Snowflake, through your dbt models, to your Hex dashboard. Before the agent changes anything, it maps the _blast radius_ — every downstream table and dashboard the change would touch.
* **Graph-based planning with flexible computation.** Plan complex data tasks with parallel agents from a quick analysis to days-long modeling experiments to run across your machine and remote CPU/GPU nodes.
* **A living knowledge base.** Alkera learns your schema docs, trusted queries, and the tribal conventions that never make it into documentation — written by both agents and humans, with humans verifying what the agent adds.
* **Production protection.** Fine-grained permissions over every tool, including bash and SQL. Block a seemingly innocent SQL query with a dangerous UPDATE hidden away in a subexpression. Enforce OAuth to connect your warehouses to maintain existing data permissions.

# **Try it**

Download Alkera at <https://alkera.ai> or read the docs at <https://docs.alkera.ai>. For data engineering, point it at your stack and **watch it trace a change through your pipeline**, lighting up everything downstream. For data analysis and data science, have it **spin up parallel research agents** to explore your data. Reach out to [contact@alkera.ai](mailto:contact@alkera.ai) to see how we can tailor Alkera to your specific data apps/tools and computing environment.

# **Our team**

* Andrew Tran studied CS at Yale. At Yale, he trained LLMs to reason over multi-modal biological data. At Ramp and Hudson River Trading, he worked closely with data teams to build out ergonomic tooling for data engineers and researchers.
* Rick Gao studied CS at Yale. He was previously at Verition Fund Management, where he worked with internal data teams and counterparties to develop ingestion pipelines and internal financial models.
* Tony Li studied CS and Math at Yale. During his time at Carthage Capital and ByteDance, he worked with data engineering teams to build data pipelines, data analysis, and agentic tooling.

# **Our ask**

If you:

* perform data engineering work on production pipelines with tools like dbt and Apache Airflow
* perform data analysis/data science work in Python/R and with tools like Jupyter notebooks
* manage a data team – engineers, analysts, or scientists
* want to enable non-data experts to create data insights

Check out <https://alkera.ai> and reach out at [contact@alkera.ai](mailto:contact@alkera.ai). We’d love to showcase a demo, learn more about your data teams’ pain points, and share more about how Alkera can help supercharge them.

name: Graphify Labs
long_description:
Graphify is a Knowledge Graph control plane for enterprise software. The open-source tool has 116K+ GitHub stars and 6.5M+ downloads, and is used in production by engineers at Shopify, Datadog, JP Morgan, American Express, Harvey, Automation Anywhere, and Vanguard.

On top of that graph, our enterprise layer reviews every pull request and formally verifies each code change: it proves the new behavior matches the old, or hands back the exact input that breaks it. That makes it built for the changes teams fear most, like refactors, framework upgrades, and large-scale migrations, where you need proof that nothing broke, not a guess.

The graph updates itself as the code changes and keeps context instead of forgetting it, so your whole team and their coding agents work from one shared, always-current view of the codebase instead of a thousand private threads.

It runs entirely inside your perimeter, fully air-gapped on-premise or self-hosted in your own cloud, so no code or data ever leaves your environment.
one_liner: On-device Knowledge Graph engine for Enterprise Software

Published researcher and author of The Memory Layer. MS Data Science, University of Birmingham; thesis on knowledge-graph-powered RAG systems achieving a 50% improvement in retrieval and 67% reduction in hallucinations.

launches.title: Graphify Labs: Knowledge Graph Engine for Enterprises 🧠
launches.tagline: Shared memory of your codebase, for humans and agents.
launches.body:
Hey everyone, I'm [Safi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/safi-shamsi/), founder and CEO of [Graphify Labs](https://www.linkedin.com/company/graphify-labs/).

For fifty years, the hard part of software was writing it. AI flipped that overnight. It writes more code than any team can read, and a lot of it is slop. That leaves two **hard problems**: no one can hold the whole codebase in their head, and no one can be sure an AI's change didn't quietly break something. **Graphify solves both.**

**By the numbers**

\- **108K+ GitHub stars**: one of the top five open-source projects ever from a YC company, and the first to cross 100K⭐ mid-batch

\- **5M+ downloads** of the open-source engine

\- **6,000+ signups** on the platform in its first weeks

\- Enterprises already running it in production

**The memory.** One shared, always-current knowledge graph of your whole codebase, across every language and every repo, plus its docs and tickets, so a change in one service shows its impact across all the others. Instead of grepping through files one at a time, your engineers and their AI agents trace how everything connects, who calls what and what a change touches, and answer questions across the entire system, at a **fraction of the tokens**. Agents connect over a single **MCP endpoint**, so the graph works inside Claude Code, Cursor, and every major coding tool. It groups the code into communities, the real subsystems, so teams can plan, onboard, and understand the architecture across the whole **SDLC**.

**The proof.** Graphify reviews every pull request, including changes that span **multiple repositories**, and verifies each one. It writes and runs a test that reproduces the bug, proves the new code behaves exactly like the old, or hands back the exact input that breaks it. Most AI reviewers just have one model comment on another model's code, which is still a guess. **Graphify proves its findings**, because it runs on a real **code graph and formal verification**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111176&key=user_uploads/3674994/e7f719ea-bca0-4c12-a922-12c728426dd4)

**It learns.** Graphify remembers what your team ships and what it rejects, and feeds that back in, so its reviews get sharper over time and stop flagging what your team has already decided is fine.

> Migrating a large codebase with AI is like changing a train's engine while it is moving. Graphify lets you do it without stopping the train, and proves the new version does exactly what the old one did.

**Here's the launch film**:

<https://youtu.be/nvJ1M_GRj8Q>\
\
It also proposes a fix and keeps it only if it re-verifies through the fix loop. Graphify connects to **Jira, Linear, and Sentry** so it knows the ticket a change should satisfy and the production bug it should resolve.

The enterprise layer runs on-prem, so your code never leaves your environment.

**The founder.** [Safi Shamsi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/safi-shamsi/) is a published knowledge graph researcher and the author of The Memory Layer. His research on knowledge-graph retrieval improved retrieval 50% and cut hallucinations 67%. Now he's applying that work to one of the hardest problems in software: giving every engineer and AI agent a shared memory of the codebase, and a way to prove their changes still work.

Soon every line of software will be written or reviewed by an agent. That software will need a memory of itself and proof that it works. **We're building both.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111176&key=user_uploads/3674994/439244a1-338f-46cc-8594-b7c2a74bffcb)

**The ask:** Before September 10 we're taking 10 design partners: a free 14-day build where we deploy the enterprise graph on-prem, with your team \
**Reach us at [founders@graphify.com](mailto:founders@graphify.com)**

**Dig in**

**- Run it yourself: [https://app.graphify.com](https://app.graphify.com)**

**- Open-source engine: [https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify)**

**- Docs: [https://graphify.com/docs](https://graphify.com/docs)**

**- Benchmarks and methodology: [https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/v8/BENCHMARKS.md](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/v8/BENCHMARKS.md)**

name: Vendo
long_description:
Vendo is the customization layer that lets your users build their own features and micro-apps directly on top of your product. Rather than waiting on an ever-growing feature backlog, your users can personalize the product to exactly how they work, create their own automations, and integrate hundreds of external tools, all without your team writing a line of code.

Everything runs on your existing API, renders natively in your own theme and components, and executes inside secure sandboxes within your existing security guardrails, so your source code is never touched. Companies can plug Vendo into an agent they already have, or deploy a production-ready agent complete with the ability to take actions in the product, generate UI, and draw on a built-in knowledge base. Vendo is open source and installs with a single command, and we work closely with teams to get it running for their product.

launches.title: Vendo: Let Your Users Build Their Own Features on Top of Your Product
launches.tagline: Vendo is the customization layer that lets your users build their own features and micro-apps on top of your product, within your brand and guardrails.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Nour and Yousef, co-founders of Vendo.

**TL;DR:** Vendo is the customization layer that lets your users build their own features and micro-apps right inside your product, on your existing API and within your brand and guardrails.. Plug it into the agent you already have, or drop in a production-ready one, with a single command. It's open source.

**Try it now:** [vendo.run](http://vendo.run) \
**Star us on Github**: <https://github.com/runvendo/vendo>

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JjtDhA7DZw8>

## **The Problem**

Every product team is drowning in the same thing: a feature backlog that never ends. Different customers want different things, and you can't build a thousand versions of your product. So most requests sit in a board for months, and the customer who asked churns quietly because your product doesn't do the one thing they needed.

The AI wave made this worse, not better. Everyone knows their product should be agent-native, but building a real agent (one that can take actions, generate UI, remember context, and stay inside your security guardrails) takes serious engineering hours and ongoing maintenance. So most teams ship a chatbot bolted to the corner of the screen and call it AI. Users don't want another chatbot. They want your product to do the exact thing they need.

## **How Vendo Works**

Vendo installs into your product with one command. It reads your theme, your components, and your API surface. From then on, your users can describe what they want in plain English and Vendo builds it for them, live, inside your app:

* **Personalize the product** to exactly how each user works, in your own design system.
* **Build automations** that run on a schedule and take real actions in your product.
* **Pull in hundreds of external tools**, so the workflow doesn't stop at your app's edge.

Everything runs in secure sandboxes and inside your existing security guardrails. The agent only ever has the same access the user has, so it can't do anything they couldn't already do themselves, and your source code never gets touched.

You can plug Vendo into the agent you already have, or get a production-ready one out of the box with actions, UI generation, and a knowledge base included. It's completely open source, and it takes one command to install and push live to your users.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106667&key=user_uploads/2705364/5b5c05c6-3415-4d23-bf67-a779d56456c7)

## **Who We Are**

We're a Stanford and Berkeley team who’ve known each other since kindergarten and previously built in-store AI shopping assistants for retailers.

* **Nour (CEO)** studied Mechanical Engineering at Berkeley and interned as a mechanical design engineer. Before startups, he played professional academy soccer for the San Jose Earthquakes for 7 years.

name: HyperProbe

With tools like Cursor and Claude Code, writing software is no longer the bottleneck. Debugging is. Agents cannot fix production crashes using logs and traces that were sized for human eyeballs. The gap is missing data.

HyperProbe allows agents to debug live software autonomously. Our SDK drops non-breaking probes straight into running services to read exact variable states from memory at the moment of failure, instead of reasoning backwards from flat logs.

Zero redeploys. Under 1% CPU overhead. Automatic PII redaction.

We turn 4-hour production war rooms into 10-minute automated resolutions. As agents write and operate more of the world's software, HyperProbe is the runtime observability layer that lets them understand what they built.

launches.title: Hyperprobe: On-call Agent for engineering teams
launches.tagline: The fastest way for coding agents to debug incidents live in production.
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR:** AI writes most of our code now. Debugging it when it breaks in production is still slow, because the value that explains the failure was never logged. HyperProbe is an on-call agent for engineering teams. It takes an open incident to a confirmed root cause by dropping read-only probes into your running service and capturing the exact variable state logs don't have. No redeploys, no restarting the app. \
\
📹 **Launch Video: [https://youtu.be/QtaZrQ8_Uk8](https://youtu.be/QtaZrQ8_Uk8)**

**🚧 The Problem**

Team ships faster than ever with agents that write most of our code. This is already shrinking the useful context engineers need to debug AI written code. Not helped by the limited telemetry added in the same code by AI. So when something breaks in prod, the first instinct for engineers is to open logs or throw them to agents. But if the line you are looking for is not there, agents will start guessing the root cause on limited data, forcing engineers to collect more logs by redeploys.

The result: our best engineers become our on-call team, incidents stay open longer, and patches come from data that never capture production context, so issues recur.

You can see where that leads. In September last year, a public fintech in India paid out $5 million after failed transactions were incorrectly marked successful. NYSE the same year miscalculated price bands for 40 symbols, printing trades so wrong they had to be reversed. Same pattern: the code ran clean, wrote the wrong state, and neither logs nor traces could show it.

 ✅ **What Hyperprobe does**

HyperProbe gives engineering teams an on-call agent that works the incident and takes it to a confirmed root cause, live in production.

* **Plan:** the agent picks up the alert from PagerDuty, Datadog, or Slack, then reads your logs and traces to locate the file and line. The easy incidents resolve right here.
* **Probe:** logs not enough? places read-only virtual breakpoints on the suspect lines and captures the exact variable state live, across services. No redeploys, no restarts. 
* **Confirm:** the diagnosis is verified against real captured evidence, not a guess. Your engineer gets a confirmed RCA and commits the fix.

There are two pieces. An SDK that runs inside your service, and an MCP server your coding agent talks to. The SDK is what makes setting probes (virtual breakpoints, log or metric) possible without a redeploy. 

### **🔍 A few examples**

* **An intermittent 500 that won't reproduce locally:** catch it live with full variable state 
* **A third-party API misbehaving:** see the exact payload and response
* **A function returns a wrong value with no error:** see what it computed and why
* **Anything that only happens in prod:** stop redeploying with console.logs

🚀 **The team**

We've both lived this problem. Shailendra ran production at scale. Karan was a senior architect at a SaaS company. Before this, both spent three years building production SDKs for a testing product, learning the hard parts of pulling real runtime state out of a running service without breaking it.

Every incident we watched came down to the same question: what was the actual value at the moment it broke. Nobody built it for the way engineers debug with coding agents now. So we did.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110401&key=user_uploads/3173209/ddf3d8d0-2bd4-4a8c-9547-fa5ea2496469)

### **🎁 Why now**

For thirty years the expensive part of software was writing it, and every tool got built for that. Generation is now nearly free, but the cost didn't disappear. It moved downstream, to figuring out why the generated code broke in production.

And that system is now mostly code no human wrote or holds in their head. When it breaks, the engineer has less context than ever, and their first move is already to hand it to the coding agent. That agent only has your logs and traces, so it guesses. We give it the evidence instead, captured live from the running code at the point of failure.

### **🙏 Our ask**

* If you're an engineer tired of the redeploy loop, debugging code you didn't write at 2 AM, try it on your own service.**,** first investigation in 10 min:[ https://docs.hyperprobe.co/quickstart](https://docs.hyperprobe.co/quickstart)
* If your best engineers have become your on-call team and you want that fixed, let us work one real incident from your stack, free: <https://calendly.com/shailendra-hyperprobe/30min>

**TL;DR:** OpenRelay is building an Inference Delivery Network (IDN) on top of its CDN for GPUs. We provide one entrypoint for inference across every chip. 

Send us a workload and we’ll cut your costs up to 20% by running it through our network, balancing the best available accelerator (NVIDIA, TPU, Trainium, AMD) across clouds and handing back a single endpoint. You never pick the hardware, chase quotas, or rebuild your stack per provider. And if you run GPUs or other AI accelerators (an NVIDIA cluster, TPUs, a reserved fleet), you can plug your capacity into our rails and we'll bring the inference demand. Get started [here](https://openrelay.inc/).

P.S. sign up for our Luma page to be notified of our Launch Party!

<https://luma.com/s6x8cx5x>

\
<https://youtu.be/7uNhqcjBXJg>

## The Team

Hey guys! We're **Jaden and Prashant**, the founders of OpenRelay. We came at the same problem from opposite sides.

* Jaden built a half-megawatt data center at 20 from a warehouse shell, then joined Voltage Park early, where he ran virtualization and helped stand up HPC.
* Prashant built accelerator infra at AWS, where he ran custom model deployments and wrote custom kernels to squeeze out Trainium performance.

 

We kept seeing the same thing: there's more AI compute than ever, and you still can't reach it. We left our jobs to fix that.

## The Problem

Compute is everywhere; liquidity is nowhere. Accelerators are scattered across dozens of clouds, chip vendors, and operators, each behind its own quotas, drivers, contracts, and console. Teams that want to run inference can't reach the capacity, and the capacity can't reach them.

Running inference naively is easy; running it at scale is hard. Any operator can spin up a model on a box. Turning idle GPUs into a production endpoint (load balancing, isolation, autoscaling, failover, metering, billing) is a software platform most individual operators won't build. So capacity sits stranded behind their own front door, and developers either overpay for scarce reserved GPUs or hand-stitch a fragile multi-provider stack.

## Solution

We built one set of rails across all of it.

Send a workload (any container or model) and we schedule it onto the best-fit accelerator, attach a production endpoint, and scale it. We route to the cheapest accelerator that meets your latency and throughput targets, and we benchmark continuously. If the market can't beat renting yourself, we backstop with our own inference demand, so you’re never on the hook. 

You never pick the chip, cloud, or region; we handle routing, isolation, failover, metering, and billing across 4+ clouds and every major chip family. We're language- and framework-agnostic (no SDK lock-in), and you can drive everything from our CLI and REST API.

It's two-sided: if you run GPUs or other accelerators (a neocloud, a data center, a pay for an underutilized reserved fleet), you can connect that capacity to our rails and we'll bring the inference demand, turning hardware into a revenue-generating endpoint without building a platform yourself.

## Traction

We're **live in production**, generating 100 billion tokens a week across 22 physical locations across Europe, APAC, North America, and the Middle East running on 8 different accelerator SKUs.  

## Asks

We'd love to hear from you!

* **Run GPUs, or know someone who does?** This is who we most want to talk to: companies running their own nodes for inference, data centers, reserved fleets, even a crypto or mining cluster looking to move into AI. Plug your capacity into our rails and we'll bring the demand. Reach us at [founders@openrelay.inc](https://mailto:founders@openrelay.inc).
* **Shipping inference and tired of picking chips?** Bring a workload and we'll get you on the best available hardware today.
* **Feedback, intros, or just want to chat?** Book a call with us, or email [founders@openrelay.inc](mailto:founders@openrelay.inc) for anything else.

launches.body:
---

---

**Update:** We’ve just launched our second tool, WaveZip - a genuine breakthrough method for capturing and storing waveforms. Read more at <https://hardwareintelligence.ai/wavezip/>

---

---

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KJTH-nNl6qQ>

—

We’re Athreya and Rishov - the founders of [@hardware intelligence](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/33573). We’re here to pick a fight with the $20B industry whose debuggers suck and won’t open until an ancient license server gives it permission.

**TL;DR: Our first product, Wave, is a SOTA waveform debugger that lives completely in the terminal, built for the agentic era.** An agent can jump you to the moment a design breaks, drag in waveforms and manipulate them, trace bad signals to its source and even prove its fix against the simulation - all visual. We allow teams to build better chips in less time.

**The quick ask:** If you or anyone you know builds or verifies chips (ASICs/FPGAs), please email us! We would love to talk :)

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5nXvicwWONQ>

❌ **The Problem**

The AI boom is a chip boom - more companies and teams than ever are designing silicon. However, the reality is hardware is not software: you can’t patch a chip after it ships. A bug that reaches manufacturing can be a nine-figure mistake. That’s why **companies spend 70% of the entire chip design process just on verification**.

Hardware verification engineers run thousands of simulated tests first on their code (simulation) which typically can take **hours to days**. If one of these tests fail, debugging means reading a waveform - a log of every signal, millions of ticks long, hiding the tick where a value went wrong. It’s literally a needle in a haystack… a big haystack. It’s common for these waveform files to be several gigabytes large. **Finding this needle is the single largest activity in verification.**

**The current tools are dinosaurs.** 20-year-old GUIs behind license servers whose seats run six figures a year sold by our favorite incumbents: Synopsys, Cadence, and Siemens. Free tools are even worse.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/fd100b13-f0dd-45f0-8ee4-395edf96fcae)

Yes. This is from 2026.

Software engineers got coding agents. Chip engineers got a queue for a license and whatever this is.

👋 **What Wave actually does**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/a75818b0-b001-466b-9586-705d26deb5f9)

Wave is the first of its kind! **A fully terminal-native waveform debugger with a verification agent built in.** Wave opens files before Verdi, the industry-standard viewer, finishes its license check. Let’s do a quick dive!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/ac7e5c75-8abb-4a6d-881f-a2a9b883a8b3)

**Why the terminal?** Surprisingly, most hardware engineers are terminal power users - typically doing all their coding in Vim. We wanted to meet them where they are and make our product extremely intuitive to use - we even employ Vim bindings across the interface.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/d4063fbc-2f57-4b5c-a421-bfaa697433d6)

**Ask in plain english.** _Why is a wave x at 12.4us?_ The agent will pull in signals, act on them and trace the root cause. Everything happens in front of your eyes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/8f37dd5c-22f0-4271-b665-a096c5dbfbd2)

**Pick your fix and see it.** Wave will propose different approaches with tradeoffs. The definition of “best” in hardware design depends on the use case. Maybe you want to optimize for performance? Maybe for power? Pick the one for you! Wave re-simulates and re-reads the new waveform. See a diff of how the waveform changed and a visual indication of where the fix was implemented.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/b0875bc9-fb55-4275-8c7e-11f926bc597d)

Now watch it fix a bug end to end with Rishov!

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eTycCILW6Jk>

🙏 **Asks & Offers**

If you design chips or lead a team, email us! We’d love to work with you and speed up your RTL development.

Know someone who does? Email us!

Just want to chat about hardware? **EMAIL US!!**

👬 **The Team**

We met in our freshman dorm at Georgia Tech nearly a decade ago! We became best friends and roommates for all four years of college - after, Athreya went to NYC to work at Google and Rishov stayed to do his PhD. We promised each other that once we’re free, that we’ll go all-in and work on something we’re passionate about together. Turns out, Rishov’s deep PhD thesis on chip simulation and compilers was the perfect spark.

Today we announce our company and are roommates once again ❤️

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107661&key=user_uploads/551607/eef30a82-c606-494a-a093-3649920c7857)

—

Say hi 👋 [hi@hardwareintelligence.ai](mailto:hi@hardwareintelligence.ai) · [hardwareintelligence.ai](http://hardwareintelligence.ai)

[@Athreya Anand](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/551607) · [athreya@hardwareintelligence.ai](mailto:athreya@hardwareintelligence.ai)

[@Rishov Sarkar](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2565323) · [rishov@hardwareintelligence.ai](mailto:rishov@hardwareintelligence.ai)

P.S. Wave is just the start 👀 We got some super cool things coming to close the loop of hardware engineering.

launches.body:
We are officially launching CoArena (YC S26). Released 2 weeks ago, users have doubled every week since, and the arena went from $0 to $60,000 in revenue since. It's a live arena where the world's top Computer-Use models race to finish the same real computer task, and real people judge which one did it better, blind.

<https://youtu.be/TB_9YMYCWw4>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111689&key=user_uploads/1194042/43ddaa95-1f50-4b30-b0a4-9b085433ec3c)

**The problem**

Every AI lab says their agent is the best at using a computer, and every claim points at a benchmark score. We know those scores well: earlier this year we built the #1 agent on OSWorld (82%). That's exactly how we learned the scores mean very little. Benchmarks are static, agents memorize them, and they say nothing about the messy tasks people actually need done.

**What we built**

On CoArena, anyone can type a real task ("find me the cheapest flight," "assemble this expense report"), watch two anonymous frontier agents race it live, and vote on the winner. Names are revealed only after you vote, so the judging is blind. Every battle becomes a fresh eval no model has ever seen, and the failure cases labs never catch: prompt injection, spending money when it should ask, silent side-effects.

**What the arena has already shown**

\- Only \~66% of agent runs finish their task at all 1 in 3 dies to a failure before any score exists

\- On identical tasks, the best frontier agent completes \~87% of runs; the worst completes \~42%

\- One major frontier model times out in roughly a third of its runs

\- In \~7% of battles, human judges ruled that BOTH agents failed

\- The #1 spot on our leaderboard changed hands three times in three days, real tasks don't saturate

**What you get**

It's completely free, including models you can't use anywhere else (Fable, Sol, and unreleased previews). Run your real errands with frontier agents, keep whatever they produce, and find out which model is actually best at YOUR kind of work, not the benchmark's.

**Our asks**

1\. Use it, it's free. Bring your daily work: the flights, the spreadsheets, the research. Two frontier agents will race it, you keep the result, and your vote makes the leaderboard more honest: <https://coarena.ai>

2\. If you're an AI lab working on computer use or vision, or a robotics company building on vision, we'd love to talk. We can send you sample evals and data today: [founders@coasty.ai](mailto:founders@coasty.ai)

launches.title: Coasty: The computer-use agent that doesn't break on real software
launches.tagline: Coasty helps developers kill RPA.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Coasty gives developers a computer-use agent that reliably automates back-office work in legacy desktop software where RPA scripts and other CUAs fail. It’s achieved 82.81% on OSWorld and it’s great at automating workflows where quiet mistakes cost the most: regulatory filings, patient records, payments, and gives developers precise control and observability over its work.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3EwLfqlgDEM>\
(_The portals and the data in it, are mockups_)

**Replayable audit trail (real run):** <https://coasty.ai/share/5b3320fc-0e64-4f1b-b684-9fd6e8cd8960> 

**OSWorld submission (Coasty scored 82.81% on OSWorld Verified, confirmed by the OSWorld team, with our latest internal run at 85.60%.):**[ https://github.com/coasty-ai/coasty-osworld](https://github.com/coasty-ai/coasty-osworld)\
\
**The Problem**

Most back-office work doesn't happen in clean web apps. It happens in legacy desktop software, full of surprise pop-ups, wandering menus, and impenetrable UIs.

Today, developers automating this back-office “real” work are stuck choosing between brittle RPA scripts and CUAs that demo beautifully and score high but break on contact.

The problem isn't getting an agent to click. It's trusting it when a silent mistake gets someone fired.

### **Why Coasty is reliable where others aren't**

**It recovers mid-task.** Coasty catches its errors and fixes them mid-run. If it’s crunching on a 20-step workflow and makes a misclick at step 3, it will recover and start from the error. First-pass accuracy is vanity. Recovery keeps a run alive.

**It survives messy software.** Pop-ups, modals that steal focus, legacy desktop apps. Coasty doesn’t record clicks, it reads the screen. So when the UI changes overnight and every RPA script breaks, Coasty looks at the new screen and keeps going.

**It knows when it's done.** An agent that thinks it finished but didn't is worse than one that fails loudly. Coasty verifies its own output and leaves a timestamped audit trail you can replay.

**It swarms.** One task across forty state portals, each with its own ancient interface, all at once. Forty agents, one verified result set. What takes a team a week, is done overnight.

### **Traction**

Coasty has been verified by the OSWorld team and will be published soon, but also another internal benchmark we published (85.60%): <<https://github.com/coasty-ai/coasty-osworld> >.

We have paying customers on four continents, a few thousand active users, and we have actually grown 24x since Claude Cowork came out.

### **Why us**

We started working on this idea when models weren’t good enough for computer use (last summer), so we’ve built frameworks to test and run the perfect combination of models and harnesses to see what works in practice. Prateek worked as an ML engineer at multiple startups and dropped his Stanford admit while I did CS at Columbia and built my previous company’s entire agentic sales automation. We’ve grown with this field and have been working on it even before it got much attention, so we understand where CUAs mess up and how to deal with these messes realistically.

### **The ask**

Send us one workflow your team runs by hand. We’ll tell you straight whether Coasty can run it reliably today. If it looks automatable, we’ll build a working proof of concept on your real software before a long sales process.

name: herdr
long_description:
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them — for hours, sometimes days — across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed.

Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue — working, blocked, done, across every project — so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops.

Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.
one_liner: building the open agent runtime
